architecture_summary.operational_context: Kubernetes container orchestration platform deployed in hybrid cloud environment managing production workloads with multi-tenant isolation requirements

threat_actors.name: Opportunistic External Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Cryptomining, ransomware, credential harvesting for resale
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Exposed K8s API server, vulnerable container images, weak ingress configurations
non_capabilities: No pre-existing valid credentials for cluster access
No insider knowledge of cluster topology or naming conventions
No zero-day exploits for Kubernetes core components
No physical access to worker nodes or network infrastructure

threat_actors.name: Malicious Insider (Developer/CI)
threat_actors.motivation: Intellectual property theft, sabotage, privilege escalation
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate CI/CD pipeline access, container registry push rights, RBAC permissions granted for development
non_capabilities: Cannot directly access etcd or control plane nodes
Cannot modify cluster-wide RBAC policies without approval workflow
No access to cloud provider console or infrastructure-as-code repositories
Cannot bypass admission controller policies without code review merge

threat_actors.name: Nation-State APT
threat_actors.motivation: Persistent access, supply chain compromise, intelligence collection
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Software supply chain (compromised base images, dependency confusion), zero-day in K8s components, compromised third-party operators
non_capabilities: Cannot instantly compromise air-gapped development environments
No legitimate X.509 certificates for cluster identity
Cannot bypass hardware-rooted trust (TPM, secure boot) on worker nodes without physical presence
No insider collaboration within the target organization

attack_paths.entry_point: Internet-facing Kubernetes API server (port 6443) with anonymous auth enabled or weak authentication
attack_paths.impact: Unauthenticated cluster admin access, full control over all workloads and secrets
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: K8s API server is frequently exposed; CVE-2020-8554, CVE-2021-25741 demonstrate real-world exploitability

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious or compromised base image pushed to registry, bypassing image scanner via obfuscation
attack_paths.impact: Malicious code executes on worker nodes when pod scheduled, lateral movement via container runtime
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Image scanner may miss novel malware; dependency confusion and typosquatting attacks are prevalent

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised developer credentials or service account token with excessive RBAC bindings
attack_paths.impact: Escalation from namespace-scoped to cluster-admin, bypassing admission controller restrictions
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Overprivileged service accounts are common; token theft via pod compromise is trivial (T1528)

attack_paths.entry_point: etcd exposed on network without mutual TLS, or backup files accessible via misconfigured PV
attack_paths.impact: Full cluster state disclosure: all secrets, configmaps, service account tokens, network policies
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: etcd encryption at rest often not enabled; network segmentation failures expose etcd ports (2379/2380)

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious pod spec admitted by admission controller (e.g., privileged, hostPath, hostNetwork)
attack_paths.impact: Container escape to host, access to node credentials, lateral movement to other pods via crictl
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Admission controllers often permissive; PSP deprecated, Pod Security Standards not enforced

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised pod with service account token querying API server for endpoints, secrets, nodes
attack_paths.impact: Reconnaissance of cluster topology, identification of high-value targets (databases, admin pods)
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Default service account automounted; RBAC often allows broad read access to resources

attack_paths.technique_name: Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure: Create Snapshot
attack_paths.entry_point: Attacker with PVC create/delete permissions snapshots persistent volumes containing database files
attack_paths.impact: Data exfiltration via snapshot copy to attacker-controlled storage account, ransomware encryption
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: CSI drivers often permit snapshot operations; RBAC for snapshot APIs frequently over-permissive

attack_paths.entry_point: Attacker with etcd write access (via compromised controller manager or direct etcd client) issues delete range
attack_paths.impact: Cluster state destruction, permanent loss of secrets and configuration, denial of service
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires deep access; but etcdctl snapshot restore can recover if backups exist

attack_paths.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Command and Control Channel
attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised workload establishes encrypted tunnel via service mesh sidecar to external C2
attack_paths.impact: Stealthy data exfiltration bypassing network policy egress controls, blending with legitimate mTLS traffic
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Service mesh encrypts all traffic; network policy engine cannot inspect payload without sidecar cooperation

attack_paths.entry_point: Malicious mutating webhook registered by compromised controller manager modifies pod specs at admission time
attack_paths.impact: Silent injection of malicious sidecars, environment variables, or volume mounts into all new pods
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires control plane compromise; but webhook registration is a known persistence mechanism (T1546.013)

mitigations.control_name: Identities and credentials are issued, managed, verified, revoked, and audited for authorized devices, users, and processes
Integrity checking mechanisms are used to verify software, firmware, and information integrity
Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process
A baseline configuration of information technology/industrial control systems is created and maintained
Monitor and Block Unauthorized Network Traffic
The network is monitored to detect potential cybersecurity events
Establish and Maintain a Secure Application Development Process

findings.severity_rationale: Unauthenticated API server exposure grants immediate cluster-admin to any network attacker; no mitigations fully implemented
Supply chain compromise via container registry bypasses perimeter controls; image scanner not configured for signature verification
Overprivileged service accounts and weak RBAC allow trivial privilege escalation from any compromised pod
etcd unencrypted at rest and exposed on network enables full cluster state disclosure including all secrets
Admission controller permits privileged pods enabling container escape and host compromise
Default service account automount and permissive RBAC enable broad reconnaissance from any pod
CSI snapshot permissions allow data exfiltration via volume snapshots to external storage
etcd write access enables cluster destruction; backups exist but recovery time objective untested
Service mesh mTLS encrypts C2 traffic preventing network policy inspection; no application-layer monitoring
Mutating webhook compromise allows persistent silent injection into all workloads; no webhook integrity verification

agentic.blast_radius: Cluster-wide workload deployment, secret access within RBAC bounds, persistent volume provisioning
human_oversight_points: Manual approval for production namespace deployments
